label: EdgeRouter 4
description: EdgeRouter 4 (ER-4) - 3x 10/100/1000 RJ45 + 1x 1G SFP (eth3 in EdgeOS). AC-powered, no PoE. 13 W max.
notes: Ubiquiti sources read 2026-11-19: tech-spec page https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/er-4 (200, 575,010 B) and store page https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/er-4 (200, 323,081 B), which print the same table. **Networking interface (3) 10/100/1000 RJ45 ports, (1) 1 Gbps SFP port; Management interface (1) RJ45 serial port (4) Ethernet ports; Power method Universal AC power cord (C13), 30W; Power supply Internal AC/DC power adapter; Supported voltage range 100-240V AC; Max. power consumption 13W.** No PoE anywhere: the page has no PoE row at all, so the three copper ports are declared `poeIn: false` rather than left to the engine's PD guess - an AC only router cannot be powered down a cable. No datasheet: dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgeRouter_4_DS.pdf answers 200 with the 609,911-byte tech-specs front page, so every figure above is tech-spec-only. The store page corroborates; its `PoE` rows are absent, not empty. Merged 2026-11-27: devices/ubiquiti/edgerouter4.json was a second spec of this same box (model "EdgeRouter-4", same tech-spec page, same four interfaces), so the palette listed "EdgeRouter 4" twice under two model strings that the duplicate check cannot see (ubiquiti|er4 vs ubiquiti|edgerouter4). The surviving file is this one because every other EdgeRouter spec in the catalogue is filed under the vendor SKU (er-6p, er-10x, er-12, ER-X, ER-X-SFP) and both Ubiquiti URLs end in /er-4; the retired string "EdgeRouter-4" is kept as an alias so it still finds the hardware. What the merge brought over: the `poeIn: false` declarations on eth0-eth2 (the tech-spec page lists the power method as "Universal AC power cord (C13)" and has no PoE row at all, so a reader is told the copper ports cannot power the box), the 10M floor in their speedCaps ("(3) 10/100/1000 RJ45 ports"), and the capability rows http-server/firewall/dhcp-client that only the retired copy declared. Port names follow the catalogue convention for this vendor - copper eth0..eth2, cages sfpN - so the SFP is `sfp1` here even though EdgeOS exposes it as eth3; the cage, its 1G-only rate and the fact that it is not shared with a copper port come from the same row, "(1) 1 Gbps SFP port".
